item.title: How to check if a value is NaN in JavaScript
item.description: Checking for NaN values is crucial for input validation, error handling, and mathematical operations in JavaScript applications. As the creator of CoreUI, I’ve implemented NaN checking extensively in components like calculators, form validators, and data processors. The most accurate and recommended approach is Number.isNaN(), which performs a strict NaN check without type coercion. This method is precise, avoids the common pitfalls of the older isNaN() function, and is supported in all modern browsers.
